⇒ x8 + 1 = 3842x4

**∴ The value of given equation is 0.**

questions.question: The radius of a solid metallic sphere is equal to 15 cm. It is melted and drawn into a long wire of radius 15 mm having uniform cross-section. Find the length of the wire.

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Volume of melted Sphere = Volume of cylindrical Wire ⇒ L = Volume of sphere ÷ Area of cross-section.

Radius of wire (r) = 15 mm = 1.5 cm.

L = (4/3 × π × R³) ÷ (π × r²)

L = (4/3 × 15³) ÷ 1.5² = 4500 ÷ 2.25 = 2000 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 2000 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Radius of solid metallic sphere (R) = 15 cm

Radius of wire (r) = 15 mm = 1.5 cm

**Formula Used:**

Volume of Sphere = 4/3 × π × R³

Volume of Cylinder (Wire) = π × r² × L

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8892c46072172945a09617046f096f2d63cee3bdcdbb890154c2f2e077de8214.png] 

**Calculations:**

Since the sphere is melted to form the uniform wire, their volumes must be equal.

⇒ Volume of Sphere = Volume of Wire

⇒ 4/3 × π × R³ = π × r² × L

⇒ 4/3 × 15³ = 1.5² × L

⇒ 4/3 × 3375 = 2.25 × L

⇒ 4500 = 2.25 × L

⇒ L = 4500 ÷ 2.25

⇒ L = 2000 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 2000 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Conservation of Volume

Whenever a solid metallic object is melted and recast into another geometric form, the total volume remains strictly constant assuming no material is lost in the process.

Volume of a Cylinder

A wire is typically considered a very long cylinder. The volume of a solid cylinder of radius r and length (or height) h is given by V = π × r² × h.

Volume of a Sphere

The total internal volume of a solid 3D sphere of given radius R is calculated using the formula V = 4/3 × π × R³.

• It is named after the **French mathematician and physicist Andre Marie Ampere** considered** the father of electromagnetism **along with** Danish physicist Hans Christian Orsted.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**__Volt__

__
 
• **The volt (symbol: V)** is the derived** unit for electric potential, electric potential difference (voltage), and electromotive force.**
 
• It is named after the Italian physicist Alessandro Volta.
 
• **One volt is defined as the electric potential between two points of a conducting wire when an electric current of one ampere dissipates one watt of power between those points.**
 
• Equivalently, it is the potential difference between two points that will impart one joule of energy per coulomb of charge that passes through it.
 
• It can be** expressed in terms of SI base units (m, kg, s, and A).**

**Kelvin**__

__
 
• **The kelvin, symbol K, is the SI base unit of temperature.**
 
• It is named after the **Belfast-born and University of Glasgow-based engineer and physicist William Thomson, 1st Baron Kelvin.**
 
• The Kelvin scale is an absolute thermodynamic temperature scale, meaning it uses absolute zero as its null point.
 
• The Kelvin scale was developed by shifting the starting point of the much older Celsius scale down from the melting point of water to absolute zero.

**Candela**__

 
• The **candela (cd)** is defined as **the luminous intensity** in a given direction of a source that emits** monochromatic radiation of frequency 540 × 1012 hertz.**
 
• It has a radiant intensity in that same direction of** 1/683 watt per steradian** (unit solid angle).
 
• It is the unit of luminous intensity in the International System of Units (SI).
 
• The candela has replaced the standard candle or lamp as a unit of luminous intensity in calculations involving artificial lighting and is sometimes called the “**new candle**".

questions.question: In which state of matter is the kinetic energy of molecules greater than the forces of attraction between them, such that they are so far apart and move independently of each other?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gas.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**Gas

__
 
• In a **gas, particles are in continual straight-line motion.**
 
• The kinetic energy of the molecule is greater than the attractive force between them, thus they are much farther apart and move freely of each other. 
 
• The gas **particles have big distances between them.**
 
• In most cases, there are essentially** no attractive forces between particles. **
 
• This means that gas has nothing to hold a specific shape or volume.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**__**Liquid**__

__
 
• The** particles in a liquid usually are still touching but there are some spaces between them**
 
• In a liquid, **particles will flow or glide over one another, **but stay toward the bottom of the container.
 
• The attractive forces between particles are strong enough to hold a specific volume but not strong enough to keep the molecules sliding over each other.

**Solid**__

__
 
• **Solids are denser than liquids.**
 
• The** particles in the solid are touching with very little space between them. **
 
• In a solid, the attractive forces keep the particles together tightly enough so that the particles do not move past each other. 
 
• Their vibration is related to their kinetic energy. 
 
• In the solid, the** particles vibrate in place.**

**Plasma**__

 
• **Plasma is often called “the fourth state of matter,” **along with solid, liquid, and gas.
 
• Just as a liquid will boil, changing into a gas when energy is added, heating a gas will form a plasma.
 
• Although the plasma state is very rare on earth it is interesting to note that our **solar system is dominated by plasma, as the Sun is in a plasma state.**
 
• Other **examples where plasmas can be found are in stars, lightning, solar wind, fusion devices, welding arcs, neon signs, aurora, nebulae, galaxies, etc.**

questions.question: GDP that takes into account the costs in terms of environmental pollution and exploitation of natural resources is called _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**green GDP.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**Green GDP

__
 
• **Green GDP** is a term used generally for **expressing GDP after adjusting for environmental damage.**
 
• In other words, **Green GDP is a monetization of the loss of biodiversity caused by climate change.**
 
• It is **calculated by subtracting resource depletion, and environmental degradation from the traditional GDP figure.**
 
• It is very helpful for managing economies as well as resources.
 
• It is expected to account for the use of natural resources as well as the costs involved.
 
• It also includes medical costs generated from factors such as air and water pollution, loss of livelihood due to environmental crises such as floods or droughts, and other factors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**__**White Economy**__

__
 
• The term** “white economy” includes all sectors that involve the production, research, marketing, and distribution of health-related goods and services. **
 
• In Italy, it is composed of public and private components, because the Italian health system is a system composed of both components.
 
• The private component involves, in particular, manufacturing, commerce, and services.
 
• The public component relates to services provided by public hospitals, general practitioners, and, more generally, all the facilities and professionals who make up the National Health Service.

**Brown Economy**__

__
 
• **A brown economy is one in which economic growth is largely dependent on environmentally destructive forms of activity, especially fossil fuels like coal, oil, and gas.**
 
• At the center of this economy are the major oil corporations as well as a wide range of companies that assist with the extraction, refining, and transportation of fossil fuels.
 
• This type of economy is rife with political corruption and is responsible for the massive levels of global warming causing greenhouse gases in our atmosphere.

**Blue Economy**__

 
• **In parallel, considerable momentum has gathered behind the current and future role of the ocean and its resources in economic development—nominally called the Blue Economy.**
 
• This has specifically focused on the potential for growth of global trade and commerce and an increased resource base for critical provisions and services such as food and energy.
 
• The Blue Economy captures a range of activities and sectors.
 
• Three overarching issues stand out due to their importance in developing sustainable blue economies, namely healthy coastal and marine ecosystems, sustainable fisheries, and pollution from land-based sources.

__
 
• **Relay race, also called Relay,** is a track-and-field sport consisting of a set number of stages (legs)**, usually four, each leg run by a different member of a team.**
 
• The runner finishing one leg is usually required to pass on a baton to the next runner while both are running in a marked exchange zone.
 
• The baton in track and field serves its purpose as passing or exchanging objects/tools from one runner/sprinter to the next during a relay race between various competing teams of four members each running against each as a team.
 
• Track and field relay normally have the **4 by 100 meter or 4 by 100-yard relay or the 4 by 400 meter or 4 by 440-yard relay.**
 
• There are other relay distances, especially during a sole relay race competition.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**__**Hammer throw**__

__
 
• The** hammer throw** is one of the four throwing events in regular track and field competitions, along with the discus throw, shot put, and javelin.
 
• The "hammer" used in this sport is not like any of the tools also called by that name.
 
• **It consists of a metal ball attached by a steel wire to a grip.**

**High Jump**__

__
 
• **The high jump is a track and field event** in which competitors must jump unaided over a horizontal bar placed at measured heights without dislodging it.
 
• In its modern, most-practiced format, a bar is placed between two standards with a crash mat for landing.
 
• Since ancient times, competitors have introduced increasingly effective techniques to arrive at the current form, and the current universally preferred method is the Fosbury Flop, in which athletes run towards the bar and leap head first with their back to the bar.

**Steeple Chase**__

 
• **The steeplechase is an obstacle race in athletics, which derives its name from the steeplechase in horse racing.**
 
• The foremost version of the event is the 3000 meters steeplechase.
 
• **The 2000 meters steeplechase is the next most common distance.**
 
• **A 1000 meters steeplechase is occasionally used in youth athletics.**

questions.question: Identify the structural formula for ethene.

__
 
• **Ethene (ethylene)** is the most important organic chemical, by tonnage, that is manufactured.
 
• It is the building block for a vast range of chemicals from plastics to antifreeze solutions and solvents.
 
• It is a group of plant growth regulators which are widely used for ripening fruits and for the production of more flowers and fruits.
 
• It is a small hydrocarbon, the **colorless flammable gas which is denoted by the formula C2H4 or H2C=CH2.**
 
• **Ethene is the IUPAC name for ethylene.**
 
• It has a **“sweet and musky” odour** when it is pure.
 
• It is the **simplest alkene and also the second simplest unsaturated hydrocarbon C2H2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**__**Propene**__

__
 
• **Propylene** also known as **Propene has the chemical formula: C3H6.**
 
• It is a** colorless fuel gas** with a** naturally pungent smell.**
 
• It is** composed of 3 carbon atoms and 6 hydrogen atoms.**
 
• It also has one double bond from the middle carbon to one of the outer carbons, and then one single bond from the centre carbon to the free carbon.

**1,2- dimethylethene**__

 
• **1,2-Dimethylethylenediamine (DMEDA) is the organic compound with the formula (CH3NH)2C2H4.**
 
• It is a** colorless liquid with a fishy odor.**
 
• It features two secondary amine functional groups.
 
• DMEDA is used as a chelating diamine for the preparation of metal complexes, some of which function as homogeneous catalysts.

• He started learning tabla from his father,** Pandit Shankar Ghosh.**

• **The tanpura or tambura, **tanpuri is a **long-necked plucked string instrument, originating from India.**
 
• It supports and sustains the melody of another instrument or singer by providing a continuous harmonic bourdon or drone. 
 
• Hindustani musicians favor the term tanpura whereas** Carnatic musicians say tambura.**
 
• **Gowrishankar Gurusawmy, Soman Pillai, Prasanna Athele** are some of the famous tambura players.

**Sarangi**__

__
 
• **Sarangi, also called saran or saranga **is a short-necked fiddle used throughout South Asia.
 
• It measures about **76 cm (30 inches) long.**
 
• The instrument has a roughly rectangular slightly waisted body and broad fretless neck.
 
• It has** three melody strings made of gut****.**

**Bansuri**__

 
• **A bansuri is an ancient side-blown flute originating from the Indian subcontinent.**
 
• It is an aerophone produced from bamboo, and used in Hindustani classical music.
 
• It is referred to as nadi and tunava in the Rigveda and other Vedic texts of Hinduism.
 
• Its importance and operation are discussed in the Sanskrit text Natya Shastra.
 
• Bansuri is traditionally made from a single hollow shaft of bamboo with** six or seven finger holes.**
 
• Some modern designs come in** ivory, fiberglass, and various metals.**

questions.question: Which is a perennial carnivorous plant of the sundew family that attracts preys and usually traps insects and then breaks them down with digestive enzymes?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Venus Flytrap.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__****Venus Flytrap**

__
 
• The **Venus flytrap is a flowering plant best known for its carnivorous eating habits.**
 
• The “trap” is made of** two hinged lobes at the end of each leaf.**
 
• On the inner surfaces of the lobes are **hair-like projections called trichomes.**
 
• These projections cause the lobes to snap shut when prey comes in contact with them.
 
• The trap will only shut when the trichomes are touched multiple times.
 
• Venus flytrap is one of the very few that exhibits motion to actively trap its prey.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****Phytoplankton**

 
• **Phytoplankton, also known as microalgae.**
 
• They are similar to terrestrial plants.
 
• Most phytoplankton is buoyant and floats in the upper part of the ocean.
 
• Phytoplankton also requires inorganic nutrients such as nitrates, phosphates, and sulfur.
 
• They convert inorganic nutrients into proteins, fats, and carbohydrates.

**Bladderwort**

 
• **Bladderwort is a carnivorous plant.**
 
• **It is found in swamps, lakes, and streams.**
 
• There are** hundreds of different varieties of bladderworts**.
 
• The bladders are traps that are a part of the underwater structure where the plant catches and processes its food source.

**Seaweed**

 
• **"Seaweed" is the common name for countless species of marine plants and algae.**
 
• **They grow in the ocean as well as in rivers, lakes, and other water bodies.**
 
• Some seaweeds are microscopic, such as phytoplankton.
 
• Some are enormous, like the giant kelp that grow in abundant forests.
 
• Most are medium-sized, come in colors of** red, green, brown, and black.**

__
 
• **R Muthukannammal is a seventh generation veteran Sadir dancer from the Indian State of Tamil Nadu.**
 
• She is the** only surviving person among the 32 Devadasis** who served the deity at the Viralimalai Murugan temple.
 
• She is** the last woman to have the ceremony pottukkattutal of dedicating oneself to God performed at the Viralimalai temple.**
 
• In the year 2022, Govt of India honoured Muthukannammal by conferring the Padma Shri award for her contributions in the field of art.
 
• The dance form Sadir, variously called as Sadiraattam or Parathaiyar Aattam or Thevarattam, is a classical Indian dance from which was reinvented, modified and rechristened as Bharatanatyam.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****Padma Awards**

 
• **The Padma Awards are one of the highest civilian honours of India announced annually on the eve of Republic Day**.
 
• The Awards are given in three categories:
 
 
• **Padma Vibhushan - for exceptional and distinguished service**
 
• **Padma Bhushan - distinguished service of higher order**
 
• **Padma Shri - for distinguished service.**
 
 
 
• The award seeks to recognize achievements in all fields of activities or disciplines where an element of public service is involved.
 
• The Padma Awards are conferred on the recommendations made by the Padma Awards Committee, which is constituted by the Prime Minister every year.
 
• The nomination process is open to the public. Even self-nomination can be made.
